title: How to Keep the Same Face in AI-Generated Photos
metaTitle: How to Keep the Same Face in AI Photos | AI Face Consistency Guide
metaDescription: Learn how to keep the same face and identity in AI-generated photos. Use better reference images, prompts and consistency techniques for realistic results.
intro: AI image generators can create beautiful photos, but one of the most common problems is that the face changes from one image to another. This guide explains how to improve face consistency while creating different outfits, poses, backgrounds and styles.
searchTerms: how to keep same face in AI photos
how to keep same face AI image
how to make AI photos look like you

problem.heading: Why does AI keep changing the face?
problem.content: AI image generators do not always treat a reference photo as a permanent identity. When the prompt changes the pose, clothing, lighting, camera angle or environment, the model may reinterpret facial features. Small differences in the reference image can also make the generated face look noticeably different.

commonCauses: Using a low-quality or heavily edited reference image
Using multiple reference faces without clearly defining the main subject
Changing too many visual elements at the same time
Using vague instructions about identity preservation
Extreme camera angles or poses
Strong style transformations that alter facial features

solutions.title: Use a clear reference image
solutions.content: Choose a sharp reference photo where the face is clearly visible. Avoid sunglasses, heavy filters, extreme shadows and excessive blur.

solutions.title: Clearly define the reference person's identity
solutions.content: Tell the image model that the uploaded person is the primary identity reference and that facial structure and recognizable features should remain consistent.

solutions.title: Change one major element at a time
solutions.content: For better consistency, keep the identity and composition stable while changing clothing, background or styling instead of changing everything simultaneously.

solutions.title: Avoid unnecessary face descriptions
solutions.content: If the model already has a strong visual reference, excessive descriptions of facial features can sometimes create conflicting instructions.

promptExample.title: Face consistency prompt example
promptExample.prompt: Use the uploaded reference image as the primary identity reference. Keep the same person, recognizable facial features, face shape, eyes, nose, lips, skin tone and overall identity. Do not redesign or replace the face. Only change the requested clothing, pose and environment while maintaining natural photographic realism.

steps: Upload a clear reference photo.
State that the uploaded person is the primary identity reference.
Explicitly request consistent facial identity.
Describe only the changes you want to make.
Review the result and simplify the prompt if the face changes.
tips: Use the same high-quality reference image when possible.
Avoid unnecessary face-related wording when the reference is already clear.
Start with simple transformations before attempting complex scenes.
Keep lighting and camera direction reasonably consistent when identity is critical.

faq.question: How do I make AI keep the same face?
faq.answer: Use a clear reference image and explicitly instruct the AI to preserve the person's identity and recognizable facial features while changing only the requested elements.

faq.question: Why does my AI-generated face look different?
faq.answer: The model may reinterpret the identity because of the reference image, prompt instructions, camera angle, lighting or major changes to the scene.

faq.question: Can AI keep my face while changing clothes?
faq.answer: Yes. Clothing changes are generally easier when the prompt clearly separates the person's identity from the elements being changed.

title: Why Does My AI Photo Look Fake? How to Make AI Images More Realistic
metaTitle: Why AI Photos Look Fake & How to Make Them Realistic
metaDescription: Find out why AI-generated photos look fake and learn practical prompting techniques to create more natural skin, lighting, hands, textures and photography.
intro: An AI-generated image can have the right composition but still look obviously artificial. Plastic skin, strange lighting, perfect textures and unnatural details are common signs. Here is how to make AI photos feel more like real photography.
searchTerms: how to make AI images realistic
how to make AI generated photos look real

problem.heading: What makes an AI photo look fake?
problem.content: AI-generated images often look artificial when the prompt focuses heavily on style but does not provide enough photographic context. Unrealistic skin texture, lighting, depth, hands, reflections and overly perfect details can make an image feel synthetic.

commonCauses: Overly smooth or plastic-looking skin
Perfectly uniform lighting
Excessive beauty retouching
Unnatural hands and fingers
Incorrect reflections and shadows
Overly sharp or artificial textures
Too many cinematic or fantasy keywords

solutions.title: Add realistic photographic details
solutions.content: Describe natural skin texture, realistic lighting, subtle imperfections, authentic shadows and believable photographic depth.

solutions.title: Use natural lighting
solutions.content: Soft window light, overcast daylight or realistic direct flash can produce more believable photographic results than vague instructions such as 'perfect lighting'.

solutions.title: Avoid excessive perfection
solutions.content: Real photographs contain small imperfections. Asking for completely flawless skin, perfect symmetry and perfect textures can make the result look synthetic.

solutions.title: Describe the camera context
solutions.content: Camera type, focal length, depth of field, flash behavior and photographic style can help establish a more coherent visual result.

promptExample.title: Realistic AI photo prompt example
promptExample.prompt: Create a photorealistic photograph with natural skin texture, subtle facial imperfections, realistic lighting, believable shadows, authentic fabric texture and natural depth of field. Avoid plastic skin, excessive beauty retouching, artificial sharpness and overly perfect details.

steps: Decide what currently looks artificial.
Add photographic context instead of adding more style keywords.
Specify natural skin and material textures.
Use realistic lighting and shadows.
Generate again and remove unnecessary dramatic wording.
tips: Do not overload the prompt with dozens of realism keywords.
Realistic lighting often matters more than adding '8K' or 'ultra detailed'.
Describe materials such as skin, denim, silk, glass and metal naturally.
Compare the output with a real photograph and identify the specific unrealistic detail.

faq.question: Why do AI-generated photos look artificial?
faq.answer: They can look artificial when skin, lighting, textures, shadows or other photographic details are generated in an overly perfect or inconsistent way.

faq.question: What should I add to an AI prompt for realism?
faq.answer: Focus on natural skin texture, believable lighting, realistic shadows, authentic materials and coherent photographic depth.

faq.question: Does adding '8K' make an AI image more realistic?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Resolution-related keywords do not automatically fix unrealistic anatomy, lighting, textures or facial details.

title: How to Fix AI Hands and Fingers in Generated Images
metaTitle: How to Fix AI Hands & Fingers | AI Image Prompt Guide
metaDescription: AI hands and fingers can look distorted or unnatural. Learn why it happens and how to improve hands, fingers and arm anatomy with better prompts and image references.
intro: Hands are one of the most difficult details for AI image generators. Extra fingers, strange poses and distorted anatomy can still appear even in otherwise realistic images. These techniques can help improve hand accuracy.

problem.heading: Why does AI struggle with hands?
problem.content: Hands contain many small joints, overlapping fingers and complex poses. When they are partially hidden, holding objects or placed close to the camera, the model can have difficulty producing consistent anatomy.

commonCauses: Complex hand poses
Hands partially hidden by objects
Hands close to the camera
Very detailed interactions between fingers and objects
Multiple people with visible hands
Ambiguous instructions about hand placement

solutions.title: Specify the hand position
solutions.content: Describe exactly where the hands are and what they are doing instead of simply asking for 'natural hands'.

solutions.title: Keep poses simple
solutions.content: Simple, relaxed hand positions are usually easier for an image model to reproduce accurately.

solutions.title: Use references when available
solutions.content: A clear visual reference for a difficult pose can give the model more useful information than text alone.

solutions.title: Regenerate problem areas
solutions.content: If the overall image is strong but the hands are incorrect, use an editing or inpainting workflow where supported instead of regenerating the entire composition.

promptExample.title: Hand accuracy prompt example
promptExample.prompt: Natural human hands with anatomically correct proportions and five fingers on each visible hand. Keep the fingers clearly separated and correctly attached to the hands and wrists. Use a relaxed, believable pose with realistic skin texture.

steps: Identify exactly what is wrong with the hands.
Simplify the hand pose.
Describe the intended hand position clearly.
Regenerate or edit the affected area.
Keep the rest of the prompt unchanged when possible.
tips: Avoid complicated finger gestures unless necessary.
Do not repeat 'five fingers' excessively throughout the prompt.
For difficult compositions, generate the main scene first and fix the hands afterward.
Check both hands and fingers before publishing an AI photo.

faq.question: Why are AI fingers often wrong?
faq.answer: Hands have complex anatomy and many overlapping joints, making them difficult for image models to reproduce consistently.

faq.question: What prompt can fix AI hands?
faq.answer: Clearly describe natural hand positioning, anatomically correct proportions and the intended interaction with nearby objects.

faq.question: Can AI fix bad hands without regenerating the whole image?
faq.answer: Some AI image tools support localized editing or inpainting, which can allow you to correct the hands while preserving most of the original image.

title: AI Photo Identity Consistency: How to Keep a Person Recognizable
metaTitle: AI Photo Identity Consistency Guide | Keep the Same Person
metaDescription: Learn how AI identity consistency works and how to keep a person recognizable across different AI-generated photos, outfits, poses and locations.
intro: Creating multiple AI photos of the same person is harder than generating a single image. Identity consistency requires a strong reference, clear instructions and controlled changes between generations.

problem.heading: What is identity consistency?
problem.content: Identity consistency means maintaining the recognizable visual characteristics of the same person across multiple generated images, even when the scene, outfit, pose or location changes.

commonCauses: Different reference images for different generations
Large changes in age or facial expression
Conflicting identity instructions
Major changes in camera angle
Heavy artistic transformations
Weak or unclear reference images

solutions.title: Use one primary identity reference
solutions.content: Keep a strong reference image as the visual anchor whenever possible.

solutions.title: Separate identity from scene instructions
solutions.content: Make it clear which characteristics must remain stable and which elements are allowed to change.

solutions.title: Control transformations
solutions.content: Change clothing, location and styling progressively rather than making several extreme changes at once.

solutions.title: Keep a reusable identity instruction
solutions.content: A consistent identity block can be reused across related generations so the model receives similar identity guidance each time.

promptExample.title: Identity consistency prompt example
promptExample.prompt: Use the uploaded person as the consistent identity reference across the entire image. Preserve their recognizable facial structure, proportions, skin tone and overall appearance. Change only the requested outfit, pose, environment and photographic style.

steps: Choose your strongest identity reference.
Create a reusable identity instruction.
Define the scene and changes separately.
Avoid unnecessary identity-altering transformations.
Compare each generation with the original reference.
tips: Keep your reference image consistent across a series.
Make controlled changes instead of changing everything at once.
Use natural photographic settings when identity is the priority.
Save successful prompts as reusable templates.

faq.question: What does AI identity consistency mean?
faq.answer: It means keeping the same person's recognizable appearance across multiple AI-generated images.

faq.question: How can I make the same person appear in different AI photos?
faq.answer: Use a consistent reference image and clearly separate identity-preservation instructions from the scene and styling instructions.

faq.question: Why does the same reference produce different faces?
faq.answer: AI generation is probabilistic, and changes in prompts, composition, lighting, camera angle and styling can cause the model to reinterpret the person's identity.

title: How to Write Better AI Image Prompts
metaTitle: How to Write AI Image Prompts | Complete Prompt Guide
metaDescription: Learn how to write better AI image prompts with a simple structure for subject, composition, lighting, camera, style and details. Includes practical prompt examples.
intro: A good AI image prompt is more than a list of keywords. Clear structure helps the image model understand the subject, composition, environment, lighting and visual style you actually want.
searchTerms: how to write AI image prompts
how to make better AI images

problem.heading: Why do some AI prompts work better than others?
problem.content: Weak prompts often mix unrelated instructions or rely on vague words such as 'beautiful' and 'perfect'. Strong prompts communicate the important visual decisions in a logical order and avoid unnecessary contradictions.

commonCauses: Vague descriptions
Too many conflicting instructions
No clear subject or composition
Mixing style and scene instructions randomly
Overloading the prompt with quality keywords
Not specifying what should actually change

solutions.title: Start with the subject
solutions.content: Describe who or what should appear in the image before adding secondary visual details.

solutions.title: Define the composition
solutions.content: Explain the pose, framing, camera perspective and important objects in the scene.

solutions.title: Add environment and lighting
solutions.content: Describe where the subject is and how the light interacts with the scene.

solutions.title: Finish with visual style
solutions.content: Add photographic or artistic characteristics after the core scene is established.

promptExample.title: Simple AI prompt structure
promptExample.prompt: Subject + identity/reference + pose + clothing + environment + composition + lighting + camera/photo style + important details. Keep the subject recognizable and preserve the requested proportions while changing only the specified elements.

steps: Define the main subject.
Add identity or reference-image instructions if needed.
Describe pose, clothing and important objects.
Describe the environment and composition.
Add lighting, camera and style details.
Remove conflicting or unnecessary instructions.
Generate and refine based on the actual problem.
tips: Write for the image you want, not for the AI buzzwords you have seen online.
Prioritize important visual information.
Change one variable at a time when refining a prompt.
Keep successful prompt structures and adapt them for new concepts.

faq.question: What is the best structure for an AI image prompt?
faq.answer: A useful structure is subject, identity or reference, pose, clothing, environment, composition, lighting, camera or photographic style, and important details.

faq.question: Should AI prompts be long?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. A prompt should be detailed enough to communicate the important visual decisions without adding conflicting or irrelevant instructions.

faq.question: How do I improve an AI image prompt?
faq.answer: Identify the specific part of the generated image that is wrong and refine the prompt around that issue instead of rewriting everything.

title: Why AI Images Keep Changing Clothes and How to Fix It
metaTitle: AI Image Keeps Changing Clothes? How to Fix Clothing Changes
metaDescription: Learn why AI-generated images change clothing unexpectedly and how to write prompts that preserve outfits, colors, fabrics and clothing details.
intro: Sometimes an AI image starts with the right outfit but changes the clothing during generation. Colors, patterns, sleeves, accessories and even the entire outfit can be altered. Here is how to make clothing instructions more consistent.
searchTerms: how to preserve clothes in AI photos

problem.heading: Why does AI change the outfit?
problem.content: AI models may treat clothing as part of the overall visual interpretation rather than a fixed object. If the prompt contains conflicting styling instructions or the outfit is not described clearly, the model may substitute or redesign parts of it.

commonCauses: Vague clothing descriptions
Conflicting style instructions
Too many accessories
Changing the scene dramatically
Not identifying which clothing elements must remain unchanged
Using reference images where the outfit is unclear

solutions.title: Describe the outfit precisely
solutions.content: Specify the garment, color, material, length, pattern and important design details.

solutions.title: Separate outfit from style
solutions.content: Tell the model which clothing details are fixed and which overall photographic style can change.

solutions.title: Use a clear clothing reference
solutions.content: If supported, provide a reference image where the outfit is clearly visible.

solutions.title: Avoid contradictory fashion instructions
solutions.content: Do not request multiple incompatible clothing styles in the same prompt.

promptExample.title: Clothing consistency prompt example
promptExample.prompt: Keep the exact same outfit throughout the image: a black fitted leather jacket over a plain white T-shirt, dark blue jeans and white sneakers. Preserve the garment colors, materials, proportions and key design details. Do not replace, redesign or add clothing unless explicitly requested.

steps: List the exact clothing pieces you want preserved.
Specify important colors and materials.
State which outfit elements must remain unchanged.
Remove conflicting fashion instructions.
Generate again and compare the outfit with the reference.
tips: Use simple, visually distinct clothing descriptions.
Mention important accessories separately.
Do not use several competing fashion aesthetics.
If only the background should change, explicitly say that the outfit should remain unchanged.

faq.question: Why does AI keep changing my clothes?
faq.answer: The model may reinterpret the outfit when clothing instructions are vague, conflicting or secondary to stronger style and scene instructions.

faq.question: How do I keep the same outfit in AI images?
faq.answer: Describe the clothing precisely and explicitly state that its colors, materials, proportions and key details should remain unchanged.

faq.question: Can I change the background without changing the clothes?
faq.answer: Yes. Clearly separate the background change from the clothing instructions and explicitly preserve the existing outfit.

title: Why AI Images Generate the Wrong Background and How to Fix It
metaTitle: AI Image Wrong Background? How to Fix Backgrounds with Prompts
metaDescription: Learn why AI image generators create the wrong background and how to control locations, environments, lighting and background details with better prompts.
intro: You can describe the subject perfectly and still get the wrong environment. AI models sometimes simplify, replace or reinterpret backgrounds when the scene contains too many competing instructions.
searchTerms: how to change background with AI
how to control AI image background

problem.heading: Why does AI generate the wrong background?
problem.content: Backgrounds contain many spatial relationships, objects and lighting cues. When the prompt is vague or contains several locations and styles, the model may prioritize some instructions over others.

commonCauses: Vague location descriptions
Multiple competing environments
Too many background objects
Conflicting lighting instructions
Weak separation between subject and environment
Changing the camera perspective

solutions.title: Describe one clear environment
solutions.content: Start with the location and its most important visual characteristics instead of listing many possible settings.

solutions.title: Specify the background depth
solutions.content: Describe whether the background should be close, distant, blurred or sharply visible.

solutions.title: Match lighting to the environment
solutions.content: The background becomes more believable when its lighting direction and intensity agree with the subject.

solutions.title: Prioritize important background elements
solutions.content: Mention only the objects that actually matter to the composition.

promptExample.title: Background control prompt example
promptExample.prompt: Place the subject in a realistic urban street at night. The background should show softly illuminated storefronts, distant pedestrians and subtle street lights, with shallow depth of field. Keep the environment visually consistent with the subject's lighting and camera perspective.

steps: Choose one specific location.
Describe the most important background elements.
Define depth of field and visibility.
Match background lighting to the subject.
Remove unnecessary background objects from the prompt.
tips: Specific locations usually work better than generic words like 'beautiful background'.
Do not describe five different environments in one prompt.
Use depth-of-field language when the background should be subtle.
Keep the camera perspective consistent with the environment.

faq.question: Why does AI ignore my background prompt?
faq.answer: The model may prioritize other instructions when the background description is vague, conflicting or overloaded with too many details.

faq.question: How do I get a specific background in an AI image?
faq.answer: Describe one clear location, identify its most important visual elements and specify the desired depth, lighting and camera perspective.

faq.question: Can I change only the background?
faq.answer: Yes, when the tool supports image editing or background replacement. Clearly state that the subject, identity, clothing and pose should remain unchanged.

title: Why Does My AI Face Look Different? Common Causes and Fixes
metaTitle: AI Face Looks Different? Causes & Fixes for Face Changes
metaDescription: If your AI-generated face looks different from the reference, learn the common causes and practical fixes for better facial identity and consistency.
intro: One of the most frustrating AI image problems is getting an output that looks like a different person. Understanding why facial identity changes makes it easier to fix the prompt and reference workflow.
searchTerms: AI photo doesn't look like me

problem.heading: Why does the AI face change?
problem.content: Facial identity can change when the reference is unclear or when the generation introduces major differences in angle, lighting, age, expression, styling or composition. The model may preserve the general concept of the person without reproducing the exact identity.

commonCauses: Poor reference image
Extreme camera angles
Major changes in lighting
Heavy makeup or styling changes
Large age transformations
Conflicting facial descriptions
Complex image compositions

solutions.title: Use a stronger reference
solutions.content: Choose a clear, well-lit image where the face is easy to recognize.

solutions.title: Reduce extreme transformations
solutions.content: Keep camera angle, expression and lighting reasonably natural when identity is more important than style.

solutions.title: Preserve identity explicitly
solutions.content: Tell the model to maintain recognizable facial structure and identity while changing the requested visual elements.

solutions.title: Remove conflicting face descriptions
solutions.content: Do not simultaneously provide a reference image and a contradictory written description of a different facial appearance.

promptExample.title: Face preservation prompt example
promptExample.prompt: Use the uploaded image as the primary face and identity reference. Preserve the person's recognizable facial structure, proportions, eyes, nose, lips, skin tone and overall identity. Do not redesign the face or substitute another person. Change only the requested scene, clothing and styling.

steps: Check whether the reference image is clear enough.
Remove unnecessary facial descriptions.
State that identity must remain consistent.
Reduce extreme camera and lighting changes.
Generate again and compare the face against the reference.
tips: Use one strong reference image instead of many inconsistent references.
Avoid dramatic age changes when identity accuracy is critical.
Keep the face visible and well lit in the reference.
Do not add contradictory facial characteristics.

faq.question: Why doesn't my AI photo look like me?
faq.answer: The model may not have enough reliable identity information or may reinterpret the face because of changes in pose, lighting, camera angle or styling.

faq.question: How do I make an AI face look more like the reference?
faq.answer: Use a clear reference image, explicitly preserve identity and avoid unnecessary transformations that can alter facial structure.

faq.question: Should I describe every facial feature in the prompt?
faq.answer: Not always. If the reference image is strong, excessive facial descriptions can introduce unnecessary or conflicting instructions.

title: Why Does My AI Image Look Too Cartoonish? How to Make It Realistic
metaTitle: AI Image Too Cartoonish? How to Make AI Photos Realistic
metaDescription: Is your AI image too cartoonish? Learn why it happens and how to guide AI image generators toward natural, realistic photography instead of an illustrated look.
intro: Sometimes an image that was supposed to look like a photograph ends up looking like digital art or a cartoon. This usually comes from the combination of style wording, rendering cues and unrealistic visual instructions.

problem.heading: Why does an AI photo look cartoonish?
problem.content: Certain words and visual concepts strongly push image models toward illustration, animation or stylized rendering. Even when the prompt asks for realism, those signals can overpower the photographic context.

commonCauses: Strong illustration or anime terminology
Excessive stylization
Unnatural skin rendering
Fantasy lighting
Overly saturated colors
Too many artistic quality keywords
Lack of photographic context

solutions.title: Establish photography first
solutions.content: Start by describing the result as a realistic photograph and then define the photographic environment.

solutions.title: Remove conflicting style words
solutions.content: If you want realism, remove illustration, cartoon, painting or animation terminology unless it is intentionally part of the style.

solutions.title: Use natural textures
solutions.content: Describe realistic skin, fabric, hair and environmental textures rather than overly polished surfaces.

solutions.title: Use believable lighting
solutions.content: Natural daylight, window light and realistic flash can help establish photographic depth.

promptExample.title: Photorealistic prompt example
promptExample.prompt: Create a natural, photorealistic photograph with realistic human skin texture, authentic hair strands, believable fabric detail, natural lighting, realistic shadows and photographic depth of field. Avoid illustration, cartoon rendering, plastic skin and exaggerated colors.

steps: Remove words that imply illustration or animation.
State that the output should be a realistic photograph.
Add natural material and skin textures.
Use realistic lighting.
Regenerate and refine only the remaining artificial elements.
tips: Do not stack dozens of realism keywords.
Use photographic language instead of generic quality words.
Natural imperfections can make the result more believable.
If you intentionally want a stylized image, do not fight the style with contradictory realism instructions.

faq.question: Why does my AI photo look like a cartoon?
faq.answer: The prompt may contain strong stylistic signals that push the model toward illustration or exaggerated rendering instead of photography.

faq.question: How do I make an AI image more photorealistic?
faq.answer: Use clear photographic context, natural textures, believable lighting and realistic shadows while removing conflicting illustration or cartoon terminology.

faq.question: Does saying 'photorealistic' guarantee a realistic image?
faq.answer: No. The overall prompt still needs coherent photographic instructions, and conflicting style cues can push the output away from realism.

title: How to Create the Viral 1980s AI Photo Trend
metaTitle: 1980s AI Photo Trend Guide | How to Make an 80s AI Portrait
metaDescription: Learn how the viral 1980s AI photo trend works and how to write prompts that turn a modern selfie into a realistic 80s-style portrait while keeping your face.
intro: The 1980s AI photo trend has become one of the most searched AI photography styles, with people turning ordinary selfies into retro family portraits, college pictures and vintage studio shots. This guide explains how the trend works and how to prompt it correctly.

problem.heading: Why do 80s AI photos often look wrong?
problem.content: The 1980s look depends on specific period details such as film grain, studio backdrops, hairstyles, clothing and color grading. Without describing these details precisely, the AI may produce a generic vintage filter instead of an authentic period portrait, or it may change the person's face while applying the retro styling.

commonCauses: Vague references to 'old' or 'vintage' without period details
Missing description of 80s-specific hairstyles and clothing
No mention of studio backdrop or film-camera characteristics
Losing facial identity during the stylistic transformation
Overly modern lighting or background elements left in the scene
Excessive color grading that hides realistic skin texture

solutions.title: Describe the exact decade details
solutions.content: Mention 1980s studio backdrops, film-camera grain, period-accurate hairstyles and clothing rather than generic 'retro' wording.

solutions.title: Preserve identity during the transformation
solutions.content: Explicitly state that the uploaded person's face must remain recognizable while the styling, clothing and background change to match the decade.

solutions.title: Use warm, soft studio lighting
solutions.content: 80s portrait studios typically used soft, warm lighting and simple gradient or curtain backdrops rather than outdoor or modern lighting.

solutions.title: Add authentic film characteristics
solutions.content: Reference subtle film grain, slightly muted color tones and soft focus typical of analog photography from that era.

promptExample.title: 1980s AI portrait prompt example
promptExample.prompt: Transform the uploaded photo into an authentic 1980s studio portrait while keeping the same person's recognizable facial identity. Add period-accurate hairstyle and clothing, a soft gradient studio backdrop, warm studio lighting, subtle film grain and slightly muted vintage color tones. Do not change the person's identity.

steps: Upload a clear, front-facing reference photo.
Describe the specific 1980s studio elements you want.
State that the facial identity must be preserved.
Add film grain and vintage color grading details.
Compare the result with real 80s studio photographs and refine.
tips: Look at real 1980s studio photos for authentic hairstyle and backdrop references.
Avoid modern accessories or digital-camera lighting in the prompt.
Regional variations such as family-album or college-photo styles can be added for more specific results.
Keep the identity-preservation instruction even when adding heavy stylistic changes.

faq.question: How do I make an accurate 1980s AI photo?
faq.answer: Describe period-specific studio backdrops, hairstyles, clothing, film grain and color grading instead of using a generic vintage filter instruction.

faq.question: Why does the 80s AI trend sometimes change my face?
faq.answer: Heavy stylistic transformations can shift facial identity if the prompt does not explicitly instruct the model to preserve the uploaded person's features.

faq.question: Which AI tools work best for the 1980s photo trend?
faq.answer: ChatGPT, Gemini and Nano Banana are commonly used because they support uploading a reference photo alongside detailed styling instructions.

title: Nano Banana Prompts: A Complete Guide to Better Results
metaTitle: Nano Banana Prompts Guide | How to Get Better AI Image Results
metaDescription: Learn how to write effective Nano Banana prompts for photo editing, identity preservation, realistic portraits and trending AI photo styles.
intro: Nano Banana has become a popular choice for photo-realistic AI image editing because it handles reference images and identity preservation well. This guide explains how to structure prompts specifically for Nano Banana to get consistent, high-quality results.

problem.heading: Why do some Nano Banana results look inconsistent?
problem.content: Nano Banana performs best when prompts clearly separate what should stay the same from what should change. Inconsistent results usually happen when instructions are vague, contradictory, or when too many edits are requested in a single generation.

commonCauses: Unclear reference image quality
Requesting too many simultaneous edits
Not stating which elements must remain unchanged
Overloading the prompt with unrelated style keywords
Ambiguous instructions about pose or composition
Skipping a review step between edits

solutions.title: Lead with identity preservation
solutions.content: Start the prompt by telling Nano Banana to keep the uploaded person's face, proportions and identity unchanged.

solutions.title: Make one change per generation
solutions.content: Edit clothing, background or pose separately rather than combining several major changes in one prompt.

solutions.title: Be explicit about what stays fixed
solutions.content: Clearly state which elements, such as facial identity or an existing outfit, must not be altered.

solutions.title: Use natural, structured language
solutions.content: Write prompts as clear instructions rather than long strings of disconnected keywords.

promptExample.title: Nano Banana editing prompt example
promptExample.prompt: Using the uploaded photo, keep the person's face, identity and body proportions exactly the same. Change only the outfit to a fitted navy blazer over a white shirt, and replace the background with a softly lit modern office. Maintain realistic lighting and natural skin texture throughout.

steps: Upload a clear, high-resolution reference photo.
State the identity-preservation instruction first.
Describe only the single change you want made.
Review the output before requesting the next edit.
Reuse the same reference image across a series for consistency.
tips: Avoid stacking multiple unrelated edits in one prompt.
Keep a saved template of your identity-preservation instruction.
Use simple, well-lit reference photos for the most reliable results.
Break complex scenes into smaller, sequential edits.

faq.question: What makes a good Nano Banana prompt?
faq.answer: A good prompt clearly preserves identity, requests one change at a time and avoids conflicting or overloaded instructions.

faq.question: Can Nano Banana edit a photo without changing the face?
faq.answer: Yes, when the prompt explicitly instructs it to preserve the uploaded person's facial identity while changing only specified elements.

faq.question: How is Nano Banana different from other AI image tools?
faq.answer: Nano Banana is generally used for photo-realistic editing and identity-preserving transformations rather than purely artistic image generation.

title: How to Write ChatGPT Image Editing Prompts That Actually Work
metaTitle: ChatGPT Image Editing Prompts Guide | Best Practices & Examples
metaDescription: Learn how to write ChatGPT image editing prompts for realistic photo edits, outfit changes, background swaps and identity-preserving transformations.
intro: ChatGPT's image generation and editing tools are widely used for turning selfies into trending photo styles. Getting reliable results depends on how the editing instructions are structured, not just which style is requested.
searchTerms: ChatGPT prompts for pictures of yourself
how to edit photos with ChatGPT

problem.heading: Why do ChatGPT photo edits sometimes miss the request?
problem.content: ChatGPT interprets an edit request alongside the uploaded image as a whole. If the instructions are vague or contradict details already visible in the photo, the model may apply an unintended interpretation or alter parts of the image that were meant to stay the same.

commonCauses: Not specifying what should remain unchanged
Uploading a low-resolution or unclear photo
Combining unrelated edit requests in one message
Using ambiguous style references without describing them
Requesting edits that conflict with the existing photo composition
Skipping a follow-up correction step

solutions.title: State the fixed elements first
solutions.content: Tell ChatGPT explicitly which parts of the photo, such as the face or existing pose, must remain unchanged.

solutions.title: Describe the edit in plain, specific language
solutions.content: Clearly describe the single change you want, such as an outfit, background or lighting adjustment.

solutions.title: Iterate in small steps

solutions.title: Reference the uploaded photo directly
solutions.content: Point to specific details already in the image so the model understands what to preserve and what to modify.

promptExample.title: ChatGPT photo editing prompt example

steps: Upload a clear, well-lit photo.
State which elements must remain unchanged.
Describe the single edit you want in plain language.
Review the result carefully.
Request a follow-up correction if needed instead of restarting.
tips: Keep edit requests specific and limited to one change at a time.
Use follow-up messages to refine rather than rewriting the entire prompt.
Reference visible details in the photo to reduce ambiguity.
Avoid contradicting the existing composition of the uploaded image.

faq.question: Why does ChatGPT change parts of my photo I didn't ask about?
faq.answer: This usually happens when the prompt does not clearly state which elements should remain unchanged, leaving room for the model to reinterpret them.

faq.question: Can ChatGPT edit just one part of a photo?
faq.answer: Yes, when the prompt is specific about the single change requested and explicitly preserves the rest of the image.

faq.question: Should I ask for multiple edits at once in ChatGPT?
faq.answer: It is usually more reliable to request one edit at a time and review the result before asking for further changes.

title: How to Create a Passport or ID Photo with AI

problem.heading: Why do AI-generated passport photos often get rejected?

Head not centered or sized correctly within the frame
Shadows on the face or background
Non-neutral expression or slightly open mouth

State the exact background color required for your country's passport photo rules.
Request a neutral expression and correct head framing.
Remove any accessories or shadows from the prompt.
Check the result against your country's official passport photo specification before using it.
tips: Always confirm your country's specific passport photo dimensions and rules before submitting.
Avoid heavy retouching, since some agencies reject over-edited photos.

Print or upload the photo at the exact required resolution and size.

faq.question: Why does my AI passport photo have the wrong background?

faq.question: Does AI retouching cause passport photo rejections?

title: How to Tell If an Image Is AI-Generated
metaTitle: How to Tell If a Photo Is AI-Generated | Detection Guide
metaDescription: Learn the common visual signs of AI-generated images, including hands, text, lighting, textures and background details, plus how detection tools work.
intro: As AI-generated photos become more realistic, it is increasingly useful to know what visual clues can reveal that an image was not taken with a camera. This guide covers the most common signs and how detection tools approach the problem.
searchTerms: how to tell if image is AI generated
how to detect fake AI photo

problem.heading: Why is it getting harder to spot AI images?
problem.content: Newer AI image models produce more realistic lighting, skin texture and composition than earlier tools, which means older detection tricks such as obviously wrong hands are less reliable than before. Spotting AI images now often requires looking at several smaller details together rather than one obvious flaw.

commonCauses: Improved realism in skin, lighting and textures
Fewer obvious hand and finger errors in newer models
More consistent backgrounds and objects
Better handling of reflections and shadows
Compression and re-uploading that hides subtle artifacts
People being less familiar with newer AI visual patterns

solutions.title: Check small text and patterns
solutions.content: AI models can still struggle with small text, fine repeating patterns and complex background details, so zoom into these areas.

solutions.title: Look at hands, ears and teeth
solutions.content: These areas remain some of the most error-prone details even in advanced models.

solutions.title: Examine lighting consistency
solutions.content: Check whether shadows, reflections and light direction match logically across the whole image.

solutions.title: Use detection tools as one signal, not proof
solutions.content: AI detection tools can provide a probability estimate, but they are not always accurate and should be combined with visual inspection and context.

promptExample.title: Self-check checklist instead of a prompt
promptExample.prompt: When reviewing a suspicious image, examine small text, jewelry, background patterns, hand and finger anatomy, teeth alignment, reflections in glass or eyes, and whether shadows are consistent with a single light source before drawing a conclusion.

steps: Zoom into hands, ears, teeth and small text.
Check whether lighting and shadows are consistent throughout the image.
Look at background patterns and repeating objects for irregularities.
Consider the image's source and context.
Use an AI detection tool as a supporting signal rather than a final answer.
tips: No single detail guarantees an image is AI-generated; look for several small inconsistencies together.
Detection tools can produce false positives and false negatives, so treat results as estimates.
Metadata can sometimes reveal the source, but it can also be stripped or edited.
Context, such as where an image was shared and by whom, is often as useful as visual analysis.

faq.question: What are the most reliable signs of an AI-generated image?
faq.answer: Small text, hands, ears, teeth, reflections and inconsistent lighting or shadows remain among the more reliable areas to check.

faq.question: Are AI image detectors accurate?
faq.answer: Detection tools can be useful but are not always accurate, and results should be treated as one signal among several rather than definitive proof.

faq.question: Why is it harder to detect AI images now than before?
faq.answer: Newer AI models produce more consistent lighting, textures and anatomy, reducing the obvious visual errors that used to make AI images easy to spot.

title: Why AI-Generated Eyes Look Weird and How to Fix Them
metaTitle: AI Eyes Look Weird? How to Fix Unnatural AI-Generated Eyes
metaDescription: Learn why AI-generated eyes can look asymmetrical, glassy or misaligned, and how to write prompts that produce more natural, realistic eyes.
intro: Eyes carry a lot of the emotional realism in a portrait, so even small inaccuracies are noticeable. Asymmetry, unnatural reflections or a glassy, doll-like appearance are common issues that can be improved with more specific prompting.

problem.heading: Why do AI eyes look unnatural?
problem.content: Eyes require precise symmetry, natural reflections and consistent gaze direction. When a prompt focuses on dramatic style rather than natural anatomy, the model may produce overly glossy, misaligned or emotionless eyes.

commonCauses: Overly dramatic or glossy eye styling
Slight asymmetry between the two eyes
Unnatural or missing catchlight reflections
Mismatched gaze direction
Extreme close-up framing that exaggerates small errors
Heavy stylization that overrides natural anatomy

solutions.title: Ask for natural eye reflections
solutions.content: Describe soft, realistic catchlights consistent with the scene's lighting rather than glossy or exaggerated highlights.

solutions.title: Avoid extreme close-ups when identity matters
solutions.content: Closer framing makes small asymmetries more visible, so a slightly wider shot can look more natural.

solutions.title: Specify a natural gaze
solutions.content: State that both eyes should look in the same direction toward the camera or a defined point in the scene.

solutions.title: Reduce excessive stylization
solutions.content: Remove overly dramatic beauty or fantasy eye-styling keywords if realism is the goal.

promptExample.title: Natural eyes prompt example
promptExample.prompt: Render natural, symmetrical eyes with soft, realistic catchlight reflections matching the scene's lighting. Both eyes should look in the same direction toward the camera with a relaxed, natural expression. Avoid glossy, exaggerated or mismatched eye styling.

steps: Identify the specific eye issue, such as asymmetry or glossy highlights.
Simplify eye-related style keywords in the prompt.
Specify natural catchlights and consistent gaze direction.
Avoid extreme close-up framing if the issue persists.
Regenerate or use localized editing to fix only the eye area.
tips: Compare both eyes closely for symmetry before finalizing an image.
Natural lighting descriptions usually produce more believable eye reflections than dramatic lighting keywords.
If only the eyes are wrong, use an editing or inpainting workflow instead of regenerating the whole image.
Avoid combining multiple conflicting eye-color or eye-shape instructions.

faq.question: Why do AI-generated eyes look asymmetrical?
faq.answer: Small anatomical inconsistencies can appear when the model prioritizes stylistic effects over precise facial symmetry.

faq.question: How do I get more realistic eye reflections in AI images?
faq.answer: Describe soft, natural catchlights that match the scene's lighting instead of requesting glossy or dramatic highlights.

faq.question: Can I fix just the eyes without regenerating the whole photo?
faq.answer: Some AI tools support localized editing or inpainting, which allows you to correct the eyes while keeping the rest of the image unchanged.

Heavy stylization overriding natural anatomy

solutions.title: Avoid extreme mouth close-ups

solutions.title: Remove vague perfection language

Compare the result with a natural reference photo.

Avoid combining wide-smile requests with heavy stylization.
Check symmetry and spacing of the teeth before finalizing an image.

faq.question: Why does AI make teeth look too perfect?

faq.question: Can I fix distorted teeth without regenerating the whole photo?

title: Why AI-Generated Hair Looks Fake or Wig-Like
metaTitle: AI Hair Looks Fake? How to Get Realistic AI-Generated Hair
metaDescription: Learn why AI-generated hair can look like a wig or plastic helmet, and how to prompt for natural strands, texture and realistic hairstyles.
intro: Hair is another detail that can make an otherwise realistic AI photo look artificial. A smooth, helmet-like appearance or unnaturally perfect strands are common signs that the prompt needs more texture-specific language.

problem.heading: Why does AI hair look artificial?
problem.content: Hair is made of thousands of individual strands with irregular flyaways, texture and movement. When a prompt only names a hairstyle without describing texture, the model can render hair as a smooth, uniform mass rather than realistic strands.

commonCauses: Overly smooth, helmet-like hair rendering
Missing flyaway strands and natural texture
Unrealistic shine or gloss
Hairstyle not matching the described hair type
Extreme wind or motion effects exaggerating errors
Heavy stylization overriding natural hair structure

solutions.title: Describe natural hair texture
solutions.content: Mention individual strands, subtle flyaways and natural texture appropriate to the hair type, such as wavy, curly or straight.

solutions.title: Match hairstyle to hair type
solutions.content: Describe the hairstyle in a way that is physically consistent with the described hair texture and length.

solutions.title: Use natural lighting on hair
solutions.content: Soft, natural lighting produces more believable highlights than exaggerated glossy shine.

solutions.title: Avoid extreme motion effects
solutions.content: Strong wind or dramatic movement can exaggerate unnatural hair rendering, so keep hair movement subtle unless it is intentional.

promptExample.title: Realistic hair prompt example
promptExample.prompt: Render natural hair with visible individual strands, subtle flyaways and realistic texture appropriate to a wavy medium-length hairstyle. Use soft, natural lighting with believable highlights, avoiding an overly smooth, glossy or helmet-like appearance.

steps: Identify the hair type and length you want.
Describe natural strand texture and subtle flyaways.
Match the lighting description to natural highlights.
Avoid extreme motion or wind effects unless intended.
Regenerate or edit the hair area if it still looks unnatural.
tips: Reference realistic hair types, such as curly, wavy or straight, rather than generic 'nice hair' wording.
Avoid asking for excessive shine or gloss if realism is the goal.
Subtle imperfections, like a few loose strands, can make hair look more natural.
Use localized editing if only the hair needs correction.

faq.question: Why does AI hair look like a wig?
faq.answer: The model may render hair as a smooth, uniform mass when the prompt does not describe natural strand texture, flyaways or realistic lighting.

faq.question: How do I get realistic hair texture in AI photos?
faq.answer: Describe the specific hair type, natural strand detail and subtle flyaways, and use soft, natural lighting instead of exaggerated shine.

faq.question: Does the hairstyle description matter for realism?
faq.answer: Yes. The hairstyle should be physically consistent with the described hair type and length to avoid an artificial appearance.

title: How to Fix Lighting and Shadow Mismatches in AI Images
metaTitle: AI Image Lighting Mismatch? How to Fix Inconsistent Shadows
metaDescription: Learn why AI-generated images sometimes have inconsistent lighting or mismatched shadows, and how to prompt for coherent, realistic lighting.
intro: A photo can have a realistic subject and background separately, yet still look wrong when the lighting direction, shadow angle or color temperature do not match between them. This guide explains how to prompt for coherent lighting.

problem.heading: Why does AI lighting look inconsistent?
problem.content: AI models generate the subject and environment together, but if the prompt does not clearly define a single light source and direction, shadows, highlights and color temperature can end up mismatched between different parts of the image.

commonCauses: Multiple conflicting lighting instructions
No defined light source or direction
Background and subject lit with different color temperatures
Shadows pointing in inconsistent directions
Reflections that do not match the described light source
Combining daytime and nighttime lighting cues

solutions.title: Define one light source
solutions.content: Specify a single primary light source, such as soft window light from the left, and its approximate direction.

solutions.title: Match subject and background lighting
solutions.content: Ensure the described lighting applies consistently to both the subject and the environment.

solutions.title: Specify a consistent color temperature
solutions.content: State whether the lighting should be warm, cool or neutral to avoid mismatched tones between elements.

solutions.title: Describe shadow direction explicitly
solutions.content: Mention where shadows should fall relative to the light source for a more physically coherent result.

promptExample.title: Consistent lighting prompt example
promptExample.prompt: Light the entire scene with a single soft, warm light source coming from the upper left, consistent with a late afternoon sun. Shadows should fall to the lower right for both the subject and the background, with a matching warm color temperature throughout the image.

steps: Decide on one primary light source and direction.
Apply that lighting description to both subject and background.
Specify a consistent color temperature.
Describe the expected shadow direction.
Review the image for mismatched highlights, shadows or tones.
tips: Avoid listing multiple different lighting styles in one prompt.
Reference real lighting scenarios, such as 'overcast daylight' or 'golden hour', for more coherent results.
Check reflections in glass, eyes or glossy surfaces for consistency with the described light source.
Simplify the lighting description if mismatches persist.

faq.question: Why do shadows look wrong in my AI image?
faq.answer: Shadows can look inconsistent when the prompt does not define a single, clear light source and direction for the entire scene.

faq.question: How do I get consistent lighting between the subject and background?
faq.answer: Describe one light source and color temperature and apply it explicitly to both the subject and the environment in the prompt.

faq.question: Does mentioning a time of day help with lighting accuracy?
faq.answer: Yes. Referencing a specific, real lighting scenario such as golden hour or overcast daylight tends to produce more physically coherent results than abstract lighting terms.

title: How to Keep a Character Consistent Across an AI Story or Comic

Different artists' styles applied inconsistently

Costume or color details not repeated in every prompt
Generating scenes in isolation without comparing to earlier ones

solutions.title: Keep the art style locked

Avoid rewriting the character description differently in each prompt.

faq.answer: Create a fixed character reference sheet and reuse the same character description and art style in every scene prompt.

faq.question: Why does my AI character look different in each panel?
faq.answer: Each generation is interpreted independently, so small wording differences, style changes or pose variations can cause the character's appearance to drift.

faq.question: Should I regenerate an entire scene if the character looks slightly off?
faq.answer: Not always. If the composition is otherwise correct, targeted editing of the character's face or outfit can be more efficient than regenerating the whole scene.

title: How to Fix AI Image Artifacts Where Objects Merge or Blend
metaTitle: AI Image Objects Merging? How to Fix Visual Artifacts
metaDescription: Learn why AI-generated images sometimes show objects merging, blending or overlapping incorrectly, and how to prompt for cleaner compositions.
intro: AI images sometimes show strange artifacts where two separate objects appear to merge, overlap unnaturally or blend into the background. This is more common in busy scenes with many overlapping elements.

problem.heading: Why do objects merge or blend incorrectly in AI images?
problem.content: When a scene contains many overlapping objects, similar colors, or unclear spatial relationships, the model can struggle to keep each object visually separate, resulting in blended edges, duplicated parts or objects that appear to fuse together.

commonCauses: Too many overlapping objects in one composition
Objects with similar colors or textures placed close together
Unclear spatial instructions in the prompt
Complex backgrounds competing with the main subject
Multiple people or items with overlapping limbs or edges
Ambiguous foreground and background separation

solutions.title: Simplify the composition
solutions.content: Reduce the number of overlapping objects and describe a clearer spatial arrangement between elements.

solutions.title: Use distinct colors and materials
solutions.content: Describe objects with different colors or materials so the model can separate them more clearly.

solutions.title: Specify spatial relationships
solutions.content: State which objects are in the foreground, middle ground and background, and how they are positioned relative to each other.

solutions.title: Edit problem areas locally
solutions.content: If most of the image is correct, use an inpainting or editing workflow to fix only the merged or blended area.

promptExample.title: Clean composition prompt example
promptExample.prompt: Arrange the scene with the main subject clearly in the foreground, a separate object placed to the right with a visible gap between them, and a softly blurred background further behind. Use distinct colors and materials for each object so their edges remain clearly separated.

steps: Identify where objects are merging or blending in the image.
Simplify the number of overlapping elements in the prompt.
Describe clear spatial relationships between objects.
Use distinct colors or materials to separate similar items.
Use localized editing to correct the affected area if needed.
tips: Busy scenes with many similar-looking objects are more prone to merging artifacts.
Adding a small gap or clear separation in the description can help the model keep objects distinct.
Check hands, limbs and overlapping fabric closely in group photos.
Simplify the background if it is competing visually with the main subject.

faq.question: Why do objects merge together in AI-generated images?
faq.answer: This often happens in busy scenes with many overlapping or similarly colored objects, where the model struggles to keep each element visually distinct.

faq.question: How do I stop AI from blending two objects together?
faq.answer: Simplify the composition, use distinct colors or materials, and clearly describe the spatial relationship between the objects.

faq.question: Can I fix a merged object without regenerating the whole image?
faq.answer: Yes, many AI tools support localized editing or inpainting, which can correct the affected area while keeping the rest of the image intact.

title: How to Create AI Baby, Future Self and Age Transformation Photos
metaTitle: AI Baby & Age Transformation Photo Guide | Prompts and Tips
metaDescription: Learn how to create realistic AI baby predictions, future self and age transformation photos while keeping recognizable facial features.
intro: AI age transformation trends, including baby-face predictions, 'meet your younger self' and future-self portraits, are some of the most searched AI photo styles. This guide explains how to prompt for realistic results that still resemble the real person.

problem.heading: Why do AI age transformations often lose facial identity?
problem.content: Aging a face up or down, or blending two people's features for a baby prediction, involves significant changes to bone structure and proportions. Without careful prompting, the result can look like an unrelated person rather than a believable version of the original.

commonCauses: Extreme age changes requested in a single step
Blending two reference photos without clear instructions
Losing key recognizable features during the transformation
Inconsistent lighting or style between the reference and result
Unrealistic skin or hair aging effects
Not specifying which features should carry over

solutions.title: Age in believable increments
solutions.content: Request a moderate, believable age change rather than an extreme jump, especially when identity should remain recognizable.

solutions.title: Preserve key facial landmarks
solutions.content: Specify that core features such as eye shape, nose structure and face shape should carry over through the transformation.

solutions.title: Blend reference photos carefully
solutions.content: For baby-prediction styles, clearly state how much each parent's features should be reflected in the result.

solutions.title: Use natural aging or de-aging cues
solutions.content: Describe realistic skin texture, hair changes and posture appropriate to the target age rather than exaggerated effects.

promptExample.title: Age transformation prompt example
promptExample.prompt: Using the uploaded reference photo, show a realistic version of this person approximately 20 years older. Preserve their recognizable eye shape, nose structure and face shape while naturally aging the skin texture, hairline and posture. Avoid exaggerated or unrealistic aging effects.

steps: Choose a clear, well-lit reference photo.
Decide on a believable age difference rather than an extreme jump.
State which facial landmarks must remain recognizable.
Describe natural, age-appropriate skin and hair changes.
Compare the result with the original to confirm identity is preserved.
tips: Moderate age changes tend to preserve identity better than extreme transformations.
For baby-prediction images, treat the result as a playful estimate rather than an accurate prediction.
Keep lighting and photo style similar to the reference for a more believable comparison.
Generate a few variations, since age transformation results can vary significantly between attempts.

faq.question: Can AI accurately predict what a baby will look like?
faq.answer: AI baby-prediction images are a playful estimate based on blending facial features and are not a scientifically accurate prediction.

faq.question: Why does an AI age transformation look like a different person?
faq.answer: Extreme age changes or a lack of instructions to preserve key facial landmarks can shift the result away from the original person's identity.

faq.question: How do I make an AI future-self photo look more like me?
faq.answer: Use a clear reference photo, request a believable age difference, and explicitly state which facial features should remain recognizable.
